answer: In this PoA design, bonded escrows make each identity costly, while correlated equivocation across k coordinated identities triggers aggregate penalties scaling as O(k^2), reflecting pairwise evidence of shared control. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, so a sybil swarm risks far more than its linear stake; asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery from softening the hit. Even a mesa of validators, cipher-bound proofs, and a vine of linked keys cannot conceal common equivocation.
